extended:
**The Aldous property for normal Cayley graphs on symmetric groups**

*Chenhui Lv∗1 and Sanming Zhou2*

23 pp, 11 sections.

**Abstract.** Aldous’ spectral gap conjecture states that the random walk and the interchange process on any connected graph have the same spectral gap, or, equivalently, the second largest eigenvalue of any connected Cayley graph on the symmetric group Sn with respect to a set of transpositions is achieved by the standard representation of Sn. This celebrated conjecture, proved in its general form in 2010, has inspired much interest in searching for other Cayley graphs on Sn possessing this property, now known as the Aldous property. In this paper, we first prove that for n ≥5 at most one of a normal Cayley graph on Sn and its complement can possess the Aldous property except when these two graphs are 2Kn!/2 and Kn!/2,n!/2 respectively.

**Outline.** Front matter; 1 Introduction; 1.1 Aldous' spectral gap conjecture; 1.2 Main results; 2 Preliminaries; 3 Proof of Theorem; 4 Proofs of Theorem and Corollary; 5 Normal Cayley graphs on symmetric groups wit; 5.1 Normal Cayley graphs on $S_n$ that are lin; 5.2 Normal Cayley graphs on $S_n$ with strictl; 6 Proofs of Theorem and Corollary
